title: Reproductive-donor screening tables retain the earlier incidence criterion
summary: Two reproductive-donor screening rows retain the earlier incidence criterion. Individual clinical duties may supply broader testing; practical effects remain unverified.
nationalGap: The 2025 consolidation retains incidence in Annex 1, partner-donation table 1 row 5 and nonpartner table 2 row 6. The separate non-reproductive rule already uses prevalence.
nationalLaw: Regulation of 23 October 2015; Dz.U. 2025 poz. 384, Annex 1; Sections 2–3.
provisions: 2012/39 Annex (2)(a)–(b), replacing 2006/17 Annex III 2.4 and 3.3; recital 3.
consequence: The express trigger differs. Necessary additional tests and individual risk assessment may nevertheless cover relevant donors. No missed test or patient harm has been established.
resolution: No later national correction or published acknowledgment of this exact EU-to-national discrepancy was located in bounded Polish and English searches.
caveat: Sections 2(1)(5) and 3 preserve necessary additional testing and individual risk assessment. Conforming interpretation or clinical standards may supply equivalent protection. This is an express-criterion comparison, without evidence of unsafe practice. More protective screening remains permitted.
review: Two agents independently read the current national PDF and authentic EU wording, and challenged alternative clinical duties. Qualified concern.

comparison.note: The amendment expressly distinguishes these terms.

recognitionNote: Bounded Polish and English searches on 26 October 2026 used the directive, national act numbers, both epidemiological terms and correction/incompatibility terms. Official health-technology material and public health commentary repeat incidence; no exact discrepancy analysis was located. This does not establish first discovery.
